root_cause: In _extract_form_body, _get_multidict_value returns None both for 'absent/empty' and for a None default, and values[field.alias] is only set when value is not None. The complement loop added by PR #12134 then copies every received_body key 'not in values' back in, so a declared Optional field sent as "" (treated as missing, default None, so skipped) gets re-added as the raw string "", which then fails int validation (422) or leaks "" instead of None.
best_solution: Track which keys belong to declared fields instead of testing membership in the result dict: build field_aliases = {field.alias for field in body_fields} and change the complement loop to `if key not in field_aliases: values[key] = value`. Declared fields are then only ever populated by the first (default-aware) loop; extra undeclared keys still pass through for model-style forms. The statement says exactly this: 'keep track of already visited field, rather than relying on the content of the values dict', mirroring request_params_to_args.
acceptable_alternatives: A processed_keys set filled with field.alias inside the per-field loop (before or after the `if value is not None` guard) is semantically identical; v4/v6/v8 all did this. Wrong alternatives: special-casing "" in the complement loop, or changing _get_multidict_value semantics.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_form_default.py: test_form_default_url_encoded posts data={'age': ''} to a route with age: Annotated[Optional[int], Form()] = None and requires status 200 and response.text == 'null'; test_form_default_multi_part posts the same to a route with Optional[int] Form plus Optional[bytes] File() and requires 200 and json == {'file': None, 'age': None}. Needs python-multipart installed in the test env.
locating_signals: Statement names _get_multidict_value, _extract_form_body, the values dict, the second complement iteration, and request_params_to_args as the pattern to copy; gold function _extract_form_body is named directly. grep for _extract_form_body lands on fastapi/dependencies/utils.py.
our_outcome_summary: Kaggle env: v4, v6, v8 PASS; v7 FAIL. v4/v6/v8 all added a processed_keys set of field.alias and switched the complement loop to `key not in processed_keys`, equivalent to gold (v4 also left a stray reproduce_issue.py, harmless). v7 produced an empty patch after 49 calls/103s. patch_labels.json marks all four resolved=False, but that is the pod eval env: every log (p_v4/p_v6/p_v8) errors at collection with 'RuntimeError: Form data requires "python-multipart" to be installed', so the pod result is an env artifact, not a patch defect.
generalizable_lesson: When a dict is used both as the output and as the 'already handled' marker, and entries are conditionally skipped (e.g. value is None), a later 'fill in whatever is missing' pass will resurrect the skipped keys with raw input. Fix by tracking handled keys in a separate set derived from the declared fields, not from the output dict. Also: when the statement spells out the fix mechanism and names the sibling function that already does it right, copy that pattern minimally, and always finish with a non-empty diff (v7 explored for 49 calls and emitted nothing). Separately, verify the eval env has the optional deps the feature needs (python-multipart) before trusting a FAIL.
